t: Sections 123(b), 607(a), and 635(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 and sections 104(f) and 202(a) of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954 are amended by striking out “Advisory Committee on Voluntary Foreign Aid” and “Advisory Committee” wherever they appear and inserting in lieu thereof “Agency for International Development”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the mention of an "Advisory Committee" signals participation by outside members. But the section only strikes references to that committee and substitutes a federal agency, the Agency for International Development, so it removes an advisory body's role rather than creating one. It establishes no consultation, hearing, comment process, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: are amended by striking out “Advisory Committee on Voluntary Foreign Aid” and “Advisory Committee” wherever they appear and inserting in lieu thereof “Agency for International Development”

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that replaces references to an advisory committee with references to a federal agency, USAID. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period or advisory role for anyone outside the government. The mention of an 'Advisory Committee' is tempting, but the text removes that committee from these provisions instead of requiring anyone to consult it.
opus.s: are amended by striking out “Advisory Committee on Voluntary Foreign Aid” and “Advisory Committee” wherever they appear and inserting in lieu thereof “Agency for International Development”
opus.b:
**Tempting reading:** The section names the "Advisory Committee on Voluntary Foreign Aid," which was an outside advisory body, so it looks like it involves participation.

**Why that fails:** The amendment does the opposite. It deletes the references to the advisory committee and puts the "Agency for International Development," a federal agency, in their place. Whatever role the committee had in those provisions is handed to an actor inside the federal government. No outside party gains a role in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that renames an entity, replacing references to an 'Advisory Committee' with 'Agency for International Development.' It does not establish a new advisory body, require consultation with outside parties, or create a mechanism for public participation. The mention of 'Advisory Committee' is in the context of removing its name, not invoking its participatory functions.
qwen_chat.s: Sections 123(b), 607(a), and 635(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 and sections 104(f) and 202(a) of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954 are amended by striking out “Advisory Committee on Voluntary Foreign Aid” and “Advisory Committee” wherever they appear and inserting in lieu thereof “Agency for International Development”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that because the text mentions an "Advisory Committee," it involves participation. However, the text is merely renaming an entity (striking out the name of a committee and inserting "Agency for International Development"). It does not establish a new process for outside consultation, nor does it describe the committee's function in a way that requires outside participation in a decision. The committee itself is being removed/renamed, and the text does not mandate any new interaction with outside parties.
